title: rwb-source-data view slice: how legacy RWB-E1-069 splits across three stories, where the two view migrations sit on the per-service sequence, and the response shape of the read operations are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-069 sections 3, 4 steps 1 to 8, 11, 12 and 13; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.1; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T2, T3.2, T3.3 and T6.3; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 9, 11, 13, 15, 29, 41 and 45; Template and Rules v1 DP-05, DP-11 and DP-15
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 1 to 7; section 7 AC1 to AC8 and the Target reading; section 11; section 12.1; section 12.7; section 13 Migrations and sequence
description: Four things this slice needs are absent. (1) The legacy story puts the four extension tables, the 16 Section A views, the 14 Section B views and the grant block in two migrations of one schema, and no source states how that set splits across an application story, a database story and an integration story, which of them owns the grant statements, or where the 30 views live once the schema is split 19 ways. (2) The legacy story places the three helper functions twice: its preconditions say V0001 created them, its flow step 1 and TSD P1 T3.2 put them in the Section A migration. (3) The two legacy migration numbers belong to one monolith sequence, and no source states their position on the per-service sequence. (4) The response field names and the problem body of the three read operations are named by no source.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-069 section 3 reads 'RWB-E1-001 is done: V0001 created the recovery tables, the three helper functions recovery.ace_to_date, recovery.ace_to_boolean and recovery.ace_mask_value, the dictionary rows and the view v_data_dictionary' while its flow step 1 reads 'takes Section A of ... into V0002__rwb_e1_069_ace_source_views.sql: the 16 views, the three helper functions and the grant block'; its section 12 reads 'No endpoint and no event. The contract is the migration set and the grant'; TSD P1 T3.2 lists the helper functions inside the Section A migration and names the two migrations 'proposed V0002, next free sequence at merge'; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 29 give the read path as a SQL view on the rwb_source_data login and name no response field; no extract states which story of the split owns which statement.
area: rwb-source-data view slice and migration split
proposed: Publish the three read operations with their response fields and problem body in RWB-P1-E1069-CON, and record in the Service Contract Catalog that the view SQL, the helper functions and the conformance test are rwb-source-data's application slice, the login, the grants, the view owner and the four extension tables its database slice, and the 19-login proof the wave 1 integration slice.

title: The ACE read is a REST contract of rwb-source-data in Architecture v5 and an in-process Java interface in TSD P1 and legacy RWB-E1-069
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 13, 15, 41 and 45; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T2 (AceSourceReadRepository) and T5.2; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A1.1; Legacy RWB-E1-069 section 12; Template and Rules v1 R3 (source precedence) and DP-05, DP-11
section: Section 1 Story; section 2 Business rationale; section 4 Flow step 8 and 9; section 12.1; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: The two sources disagree on the shape of the cross-service read. Architecture v5 makes it a REST contract of rwb-source-data on its own base, with a one-hop budget and a 2 s timeout, and states that only rwb-source-data reads the 30 views while every other service asks it over REST or a Temporal activity. TSD P1 v3 T2 and T5.2 make it the published Java interface AceSourceReadRepository ('Other modules read ACE data through P1's AceSourceReadRepository interface, and through no other path'), and legacy RWB-E1-069 section 12 states 'No endpoint and no event'. The precedence list of Template and Rules R3 puts the Architecture catalogue slides first, so the REST contract wins and the TSD wording is recorded for the next TSD version.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 15 reads 'REST GET /customers/{id}, /accounts/{id} · GET /collateral/{id}, /payments?accountId= · GET /freshness (business date) · POST /business-days/{date}/ready (Airflow)' and 'SQL ACE DB views: SELECT recovery.v_ace_* (30 views)'; slide 41 gives the first API path of rwb-source-data as '/customers/{id}'; slide 45 reads 'Only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views (ADR-010). Everyone else asks it through REST or a Temporal activity'; TSD P1 T2 reads 'Published interface | Java interface other modules call: freshness, the ACE read methods and the dictionary. No table is read across modules' and T5.2 reads 'Other modules read ACE data through P1's AceSourceReadRepository interface, and through no other path'; legacy RWB-E1-069 section 12 reads 'No endpoint and no event. The contract is the migration set and the grant'.
proposed: Adopt the REST contract of Architecture v5 slides 15 and 41 on base /api/recovery/source-data/v1 with a 2 s client budget, keep AceSourceReadRepository as the owning service's internal repository, and carry the TSD P1 T2 and T5.2 wording to the next TSD version as a change note.

title: rwb-source-data database slice: who creates the login and holds its credential, the exact grant names, the position of the three grant migrations on the sequence, and the platform sequence dependency of a Day-1 database story are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-069 sections 3, 4 steps 1 to 7, 10, 12 and 13; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T6.3; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A1.4; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 11, 29 and 41; Template and Rules v1 DP-02, DP-15 and R5.7
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 2 to 5; section 7 AC1 to AC8; section 12.7; section 13 Sequencing and Schema privileges and revokes
description: Four values this slice needs are absent. (1) The legacy story names the service role recovery_svc and assumes it exists, with no statement of who creates the login, who holds its credential or how the credential is rotated. (2) No source gives the name of a single grant privilege set: the legacy block grants one view at a time and revokes PUBLIC on all tables of schema recovery, while Arch v5 states each login owns its own schema, so whether the login also needs an explicit USAGE grant on its own schema is unstated. (3) The three migrations of this slice interleave with the two view migrations of the application slice, and no source fixes their order or their version numbers on the per-service sequence. (4) The Work Package fixes 'Depends on (build)' as None for this Day-1 database story, while the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15 carries the platform contract RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, so that dependency has no metadata row to sit in.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-069 section 3 reads 'The roles ace_view_owner and recovery_svc exist in DEV and SIT, with the names fixed in the Environment and Deployment Design' and its section 12 reads 'GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA recovery TO recovery_svc' with no statement of ownership or credential; TSD P1 T6.3 reads 'Recovery service identity | USAGE on schema recovery; SELECT on the views. No SELECT on any public table'; Architecture v5 slide 29 reads 'one login per service; grants on its own schema' and names 'login rwb_source_data', slide 11 reads 'Identity | ... | One login: rwb_source_data'; TSD P1 T3.2 names the two view migrations 'proposed V0002, next free sequence at merge' and fixes no order against a grant migration; the Work Package lists 'H': [] and 'Ready to start': 'Day 1' for RWB-P1-E1069-DB.
area: rwb-source-data login, grants and migration order
proposed: Publish in the Service Template Specification the login creation and credential policy, the exact grant and revoke list with the order of the three migrations on the sequence, and record RWB-PLT-E1044-CON as the platform dependency of every per-service database story so a Day-1 story carries it without breaking the Day-1 rule.

title: The service role is recovery_svc on one recovery schema in TSD P1 and legacy RWB-E1-069, and a per-service login rwb_source_data with its own schema under Architecture v5
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 9, 11, 29, 37 and 41; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T1.1, T6.3; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A1.2 and A1.3; Legacy RWB-E1-069 sections 3, 11 and 12; Template and Rules v1 R3 and DP-02
section: Section 1 Story; section 2 Business rationale; section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC1 to AC4; section 13 Grant block and Schema privileges and revokes
description: The sources disagree on the identity model. Architecture v5 splits the one recovery schema into 19 rwb_* schemas with one login each, states that each login owns its own schema and has no grant on any other schema, and gives the login of this service as rwb_source_data with SELECT only on the views. TSD P1 v3 T6.3 and FSD P1 v3 A1.2 still describe a single recovery schema with the recovery service identity holding USAGE on schema recovery and SELECT on the views, and legacy RWB-E1-069 section 12 grants USAGE on schema recovery to recovery_svc. The precedence list puts Architecture v5 first, so the login is renamed and its own schema added, and the USAGE grant on schema recovery stays because the 30 views stay in that schema.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 29 reads 'rwb-source-data / login rwb_source_data / recovery.v_ace_* views: SELECT only' and 'each service has one database login that owns its schema and has no grant on any other schema; only rwb_source_data has SELECT on the views'; slide 37 reads '30 views read by any module (ADR-010)' against 'Views read only by rwb-source-data'; TSD P1 T6.3 reads 'Recovery service identity | USAGE on schema recovery; SELECT on the views' with no per-service schema; FSD P1 A1.2 reads 'The recovery service identity holds SELECT on the views and nothing else'; legacy RWB-E1-069 section 12 reads 'GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA recovery TO recovery_svc'.
proposed: Rename the service role to rwb_source_data in the next versions of TSD P1 and FSD P1, state the per-service schema and the USAGE grant on schema recovery in one row of the Service Template Specification, and record the rename in the Change Register against DP-02.

title: The number of Tier 1 ACE tables is 21 in legacy RWB-E1-069 and 22 in FSD P1 and TSD P1, and the grant list is enumerated only in the legacy story
source: Legacy RWB-E1-069 sections 11 and 12; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A1.3; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T6.3
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC4; section 13 Grant block
description: The legacy story says Section A reads 21 ACE tables and prints the 21 table names in its section 12 grant block, while FSD P1 A1.3 and TSD P1 T6.3 say the view owner holds SELECT on 'the 22 Tier 1 ACE tables'. The two FSD and TSD rows are the higher sources on a technical count, but neither enumerates a 22nd table, and the grant block of the legacy story is the only enumeration in any source. This story keeps the 21 named tables, so the grant it writes is exactly the list the legacy story gives, and the count conflict is raised for the ACE team to confirm before the grant is released.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-069 section 11 reads 'Section A reads 21 ACE tables: account, payment, customer, phone, email, address, ca_relation, aa_relation, collateral, asset, efs_action, efs_action_code, efs_assignment, bucket_log_snapshot, product, branch, bot_holiday, ace_case, cfsc_mg_ssme_tdr_case, tdr_calculation and ai_recommended_plan' and its section 12 grants SELECT on exactly those names; FSD P1 A1.3 reads '1. 22 ACE tables that exist today | ACE team, read only | Reads through 16 Section A views'; TSD P1 T6.3 reads 'ace_view_owner | Dedicated NOLOGIN role. Holds SELECT on the 22 Tier 1 ACE tables, and on the Tier 2 tables once RWB-ACE-001 lands'.
area: ACE Tier 1 table list and the view owner grant
proposed: Have the ACE team lead confirm the Tier 1 table list, publish the 21 names or the name of the 22nd table in the next versions of FSD P1 and TSD P1, and keep the legacy grant block as the enumeration until then.
